comparison: Perfect match on claims C23-C26 regarding behavioral attention control. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers agree that the ANOVA results demonstrate equivalent attention across conditions, validating the experimental control. Both rate as SUPPORTED with no concerns raised.

Perfect match on claims C77-C78, C80 regarding spatial localization to pSTS. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to EEG's limited spatial resolution and speculative source localization, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED and accept the temporoparietal localization without challenge. This represents a key disagreement on the strength of spatial inference from EEG topography.

Strong overlap on claims C59, C90-C92 regarding correlation with autistic traits. Both agree the finding is supported. OpenEval notes the outlier removal (C59) as a potential limitation, while peer reviewers accept the correlation as a key contribution without methodological concerns. OpenEval also includes C60 (frequency-specificity) not explicitly discussed by peer reviewers.

Strong overlap on claims C30, C47 regarding harmonic frequency findings. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the robust statistical evidence (ps<0.001, FDR corrected) and rhythmic processing implications, while peer reviewers treat harmonics as supporting observations without detailed discussion.

Strong overlap on claims C53-C55, C71-C72 regarding inversion effects demonstrating biological motion specificity. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the statistical evidence from cluster-based permutation tests, while peer reviewers explicitly accept the BM-specificity interpretation. OpenEval does not include C52, C74, C83 that peer reviewers group with this finding.

Moderate overlap on claims C4, C58, C75 regarding domain-general step-cycle processing. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval groups these with C5, C74, C76 to discuss distinct mechanisms supported by inversion manipulation. Peer reviewers focus on the contrast with BM-specific gait processing, implicitly accepting domain-general interpretation for step cycles.

Minimal overlap on claim C62 (median-split analysis). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval discusses this as converging evidence for the correlation analysis, while peer reviewers group it with C60-C61 to affirm frequency-specificity of the AQ correlation without detailed commentary.

Moderate overlap on claims C31-C34 regarding multisensory enhancement and statistical evidence. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on comprehensive frequency-domain analysis showing different integration modes (super-additive at 1Hz, additive at 2Hz). Peer reviewers accept multisensory enhancement as expected without questioning the comparison to unisensory conditions. OpenEval includes additional claims C28-C29, C35-C36 not in peer result.

Moderate overlap on claims C41-C44 regarding replication at different speeds. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes replication strengthening generalizability with consistent statistical patterns. Peer reviewers accept the enhancement findings more broadly. OpenEval includes C38-C40, C45-C47 showing complete replication pattern not detailed in peer result.

Overlap on claims C1, C63 regarding cortical tracking of gait and step rhythms. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval groups C1-C3, C48, C63-C64 as overarching synthesis of main findings. Peer reviewers focus on C1, C28-C29, C38, C40, C63 affirming cortical tracking with 'solid evidence' from all three reviewers.

Overlap on claims C2, C48 regarding additive integration at step-cycle frequency. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval synthesizes findings from Experiments 1a and 1b. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm additive mode integration at step rhythm with C36, C46, C65 included in their evaluation.

Overlap on claims C3, C48 regarding super-additive integration at gait-cycle frequency. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval synthesizes main findings about integration modes. Peer reviewers affirm super-additive finding as core contribution with C35, C45, C67 included, treating it as well-demonstrated across all three reviewers.

Minimal overlap on claims C28-C29 regarding EEG tracking. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides comprehensive analysis of C28-C36 showing statistical evidence for different integration modes. Peer reviewers focus on cortical tracking confirmation with C1, C38, C40, C63 included.

Minimal overlap on claims C38, C40 regarding replication at different speeds. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes complete replication pattern (C38-C47) strengthening generalizability. Peer reviewers include these in broader affirmation of cortical tracking with C1, C28-C29, C63.

Minimal overlap on claim C76 regarding distinct mechanisms. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval groups C4-C5, C58, C74-C76 discussing how inversion effects support distinct integration processes. Peer reviewers group C49, C76, C84 accepting dissociable mechanisms interpretation.

Minimal overlap on claim C84 regarding unique mechanisms for natural stimuli. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting reasonable inferences but broader theoretical claims (C85-C87) go beyond current data. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the dissociable mechanisms interpretation without questioning generalizability claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims C65-C70 regarding mechanistic interpretations of super-additive enhancement as UNCERTAIN, noting that functional significance (decreased thresholds, enhanced perception) is inferred from citations rather than directly tested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific interpretive claims.

OpenEval evaluates comprehensive methodological details (C95-C126) as SUPPORTED, affirming sample size adequacy, stimulus characterization, attention task validation, and counterbalancing procedures. Peer reviewers do not provide separate evaluation of these methodological claims.

OpenEval evaluates EEG preprocessing and analysis methods (C127-C144) as SUPPORTED, affirming standard and appropriate techniques including ICA, FFT, normalization, FDR correction, and cluster-based permutation tests. Peer reviewers do not provide separate evaluation of these technical methodological claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims C88-C89 as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate acknowledgment that the study did not directly assess audiovisual integration behaviorally. This honest limitation assessment is not explicitly discussed in peer reviews.

OpenEval evaluates claims C93-C94 regarding developmental consequences and ASD marker potential as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation about clinical utility requires substantial additional validation. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these future application claims.

OpenEval evaluates background literature citations (C7-C22, C73) as SUPPORTED, affirming appropriate citation and accurate representation of prior work establishing theoretical context. Peer reviewers do not provide separate evaluation of these contextual claims.
